title: Spanish A1 to B1
subject: spanish
description: A pilot Spanish course for English speakers, from first words (A1) to telling stories and giving opinions (B1). Each unit is one lesson topic; each concept has its explanation, examples, a practice item and diagnostic probes.

units.title: Greetings and introductions
units.summary: Say hello and goodbye, use subject pronouns, and introduce yourself with ser.

concepts.name: Greetings and goodbyes
concepts.description: Everyday greetings and farewells for different times of day.
concepts.explanation: Spanish greetings change with the time of day: buenos días until lunch, buenas tardes in the afternoon and buenas noches in the evening and at night. Hola works at any time; adiós and hasta luego say goodbye.

probes.prompt: How do you say 'good morning' in Spanish?
Which greeting do you use late in the evening: buenas noches or buenos días?
How do you say 'see you later' in Spanish?

concepts.name: Subject pronouns
concepts.description: The pronouns for I, you, he, she, we and they, formal and informal.
concepts.explanation: Subject pronouns are yo, tú, él, ella, usted, nosotros, nosotras, vosotros, vosotras, ellos, ellas and ustedes. Tú is informal you and usted is formal you; ellas is a group of women. Spanish often drops the pronoun because the verb ending shows the person.
examples: Yo soy Ana y ella es Marta.

probes.prompt: What is the Spanish pronoun for 'we' (a mixed group)?
Which pronoun is the formal singular 'you': usted or tú?
What is the Spanish pronoun for 'they' (a group of women)?

concepts.name: Ser for name, origin and profession
concepts.description: The present tense of ser to say who you are, where you are from and what you do.
concepts.explanation: The verb ser is irregular in the present: soy, eres, es, somos, sois, son. Use ser for identity, nationality, origin with de, and profession, without an article before the profession.

probes.prompt: Which form of ser goes with tú: eres or es?

units.title: Nouns and articles
units.summary: Gender and number of nouns, definite and indefinite articles, and hay.

concepts.name: Noun gender and definite articles
concepts.description: Masculine and feminine nouns with el, la, los and las.
concepts.explanation: Every Spanish noun is masculine or feminine. Most nouns ending in -o are masculine and most ending in -a are feminine. The definite article agrees with the noun: el and los for masculine, la and las for feminine.

concepts.name: Indefinite articles and plurals
concepts.description: Un, una, unos and unas, and making nouns plural.
concepts.explanation: The indefinite articles are un and una in the singular and unos and unas in the plural. Nouns ending in a vowel add -s; nouns ending in a consonant add -es, and a final -z becomes -ces.

concepts.name: Hay for there is and there are
concepts.description: Hay to say what exists somewhere, with singular and plural nouns.
concepts.explanation: Hay means both there is and there are and never changes form. It is used with indefinite articles, numbers or no article, not with el or la.
examples: Hay un banco en la plaza.
Hay dos sillas en la cocina.

probes.prompt: Complete: ___ dos sillas en la cocina. (there are)

units.title: The present tense of regular verbs
units.summary: Regular -ar, -er and -ir verbs in the present, and asking questions.

concepts.name: Regular -ar verbs in the present
concepts.description: Present tense endings of regular -ar verbs such as hablar.
concepts.explanation: Regular -ar verbs drop -ar and add -o, -as, -a, -amos, -áis, -an. Hablar becomes hablo, hablas, habla, hablamos, habláis, hablan.

concepts.name: Regular -er and -ir verbs in the present
concepts.description: Present tense endings of regular -er and -ir verbs such as comer and vivir.
concepts.explanation: Regular -er verbs add -o, -es, -e, -emos, -éis, -en; regular -ir verbs add -o, -es, -e, -imos, -ís, -en. Comer becomes como, comes, come; vivir becomes vivo, vives, vive, vivimos.

concepts.name: Question words
concepts.description: Qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cómo, cuánto and por qué.
concepts.explanation: Spanish question words carry a written accent: qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cómo, cuánto and por qué. Questions open with ¿ and close with ?, and the verb usually comes before the subject.

units.title: Family and possession
units.summary: Talk about your family, possession and age with tener and possessive adjectives.

concepts.name: Family vocabulary
concepts.description: Words for close family members.
concepts.explanation: Family words have a masculine and a feminine form: el padre and la madre, el hermano and la hermana, el abuelo and la abuela, el hijo and la hija, el tío and la tía, el primo and la prima. The masculine plural can mean a mixed group: los padres are the parents.

practice.prompt: How do you say 'the uncle' in Spanish?

probes.prompt: How do you say 'the grandmother' in Spanish?
What does 'el hermano' mean in English?
How do you say 'the cousin' (a woman) in Spanish?

concepts.name: Tener for possession and age
concepts.description: The present tense of tener, and tener ... años for age.
concepts.explanation: Tener is irregular: tengo, tienes, tiene, tenemos, tenéis, tienen. It expresses possession and, with años, age: Spanish says I have twenty years, not I am twenty.

concepts.name: Possessive adjectives
concepts.description: Mi, tu, su, nuestro and vuestro before a noun.
concepts.explanation: Possessive adjectives come before the noun and agree with the thing owned: mi and mis, tu and tus, su and sus, nuestro, nuestra, nuestros and nuestras, vuestro and vuestra. Su can mean his, her, its, their or your (usted).

units.title: Describing people and places
units.summary: Describe with adjectives that agree, and say where things are and how people feel with estar.

concepts.name: Adjective agreement
concepts.description: Adjectives that agree in gender and number with the noun, usually after it.
concepts.explanation: Adjectives agree with the noun in gender and number and usually follow it. Adjectives in -o have four forms (alto, alta, altos, altas); adjectives in -e or a consonant have two (grande, grandes; azul, azules).

probes.prompt: Which is correct: 'el perro pequeño' or 'el perro pequeña'?

concepts.name: Estar for location and states
concepts.description: The present tense of estar for where something is and how someone feels.
concepts.explanation: Estar is irregular: estoy, estás, está, estamos, estáis, están. Use it for the location of people and things and for temporary states such as cansado, contento or enfermo.

units.title: Numbers, dates and time
units.summary: Count to one hundred, name days and months, and tell the time.

concepts.name: Numbers from 0 to 100
concepts.description: Cardinal numbers up to one hundred.
concepts.explanation: Numbers from 0 to 15 are single words (cero, uno, dos ... quince), 16 to 29 are written as one word (dieciséis, veintiuno), and from 31 tens and units join with y: treinta y uno, cuarenta y dos. One hundred is cien.

concepts.name: Days of the week and months
concepts.description: The names of the days and months, written in lowercase.
concepts.explanation: Days and months are written in lowercase: lunes, martes, miércoles, jueves, viernes, sábado, domingo; enero, febrero, marzo ... diciembre. Use el with a day: el lunes means on Monday.

probes.prompt: How do you say 'August' in Spanish?

concepts.name: Telling the time
concepts.description: Es la una, son las dos, y cuarto, y media, menos cuarto.
concepts.explanation: To tell the time use es la una for one o'clock and son las with every other hour. Add y cuarto, y media or menos cuarto, and a la una or a las tres for at what time.
examples: La clase es a las nueve.

practice.prompt: Translate: 'It is a quarter past two.'

units.title: Likes and plans
units.summary: Say what you like with gustar and talk about plans with ir a plus an infinitive.

concepts.name: Gustar with nouns and infinitives
concepts.description: Me gusta and me gustan to say what you like.
concepts.explanation: Gustar agrees with the thing that is liked, not the person: me gusta with a singular noun or an infinitive, me gustan with a plural noun. The person is shown by me, te, le, nos, os or les.

concepts.name: Ir a plus infinitive for plans
concepts.description: The near future with the present of ir, a and an infinitive.
concepts.explanation: To talk about plans use the present of ir (voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van), then a, then an infinitive. Voy a estudiar means I am going to study.
examples: Ellos van a comer en casa.

practice.prompt: Complete: ¿Qué ___ a hacer tú el sábado? (ir)

units.title: Daily routine
units.summary: Describe a typical day with reflexive and stem-changing verbs and frequency words.

concepts.name: Reflexive verbs
concepts.description: Verbs like levantarse and ducharse with me, te, se, nos, os, se.
concepts.explanation: Reflexive verbs carry a pronoun that matches the subject: me levanto, te levantas, se levanta, nos levantamos, os levantáis, se levantan. The pronoun comes before a conjugated verb.
examples: Ella se ducha por la noche.

probes.prompt: Which pronoun goes with nosotros: nos or se?

concepts.name: Stem-changing verbs in the present
concepts.description: Verbs whose stem vowel changes: e to ie, o to ue, e to i.
concepts.explanation: In stem-changing verbs the stressed vowel changes in every form except nosotros and vosotros: querer becomes quiero, poder becomes puedo, pedir becomes pido. Nosotros keeps the original vowel: queremos, podemos, pedimos.

concepts.name: Frequency expressions
concepts.description: Siempre, a menudo, a veces, casi nunca, nunca and todos los días.
concepts.explanation: Frequency expressions say how often something happens: siempre, todos los días, a menudo, a veces, casi nunca and nunca. Nunca can come before the verb, or after it with no: nunca como carne or no como carne nunca.

practice.prompt: How do you say 'often' in Spanish?

probes.prompt: How do you say 'never' in Spanish?
How do you say 'sometimes' in Spanish?

units.title: Ser and estar
units.summary: Choose between ser and estar, and say what is happening now with estar and a gerund.

concepts.name: Ser versus estar
concepts.description: When to use ser and when to use estar.
concepts.explanation: Ser describes what something is: identity, profession, origin, characteristics, time and where an event takes place. Estar describes where something is and how it is right now. Some adjectives change meaning: es aburrido (boring) and está aburrido (bored).
examples: La fiesta es en mi casa.

probes.prompt: Complete: El concierto ___ en el teatro. (ser/estar)

concepts.name: Present progressive
concepts.description: Estar plus a gerund for actions happening now.
concepts.explanation: The present progressive is estar plus a gerund. Gerunds end in -ando for -ar verbs and -iendo for -er and -ir verbs; some are irregular, such as leyendo and durmiendo.

units.title: Past events
units.summary: Tell what happened with the preterite of regular and common irregular verbs.

concepts.name: Regular preterite
concepts.description: Preterite endings of regular -ar, -er and -ir verbs.
concepts.explanation: The preterite tells completed actions. Regular -ar verbs take -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -asteis, -aron; -er and -ir verbs take -í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -isteis, -ieron. The written accent matters: hablé is past, hable is not.

probes.prompt: Which form is past tense: 'come' or 'comió'?
Complete: Ayer yo ___ con mi abuela. (hablar)
Complete: Ellos ___ en un restaurante. (comer, preterite)

concepts.name: Irregular preterite
concepts.description: Fui, tuve, hice and estuve: the most frequent irregular preterites.
concepts.explanation: Ser and ir share one irregular preterite: fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron. Tener, hacer and estar have irregular stems and no written accents: tuve, hice (hizo), estuve.
examples: El verano pasado fui a México.

practice.prompt: Complete: Ayer nosotros ___ en la playa. (estar)

probes.prompt: Complete: Ella ___ un examen el lunes. (tener)

concepts.name: Past time markers
concepts.description: Ayer, anoche, la semana pasada, el año pasado and hace with time.
concepts.explanation: Past time markers place a finished event: ayer, anoche, anteayer, la semana pasada, el mes pasado, el año pasado. Hace plus an amount of time means ago: hace dos días.
examples: Hace tres años viví en Roma.

probes.prompt: How do you say 'last night' in Spanish?

units.title: Childhood and comparisons
units.summary: Describe how things used to be with the imperfect, and compare people and things.

concepts.name: The imperfect tense
concepts.description: The imperfect for habits and descriptions in the past.
concepts.explanation: The imperfect describes how things were and what used to happen. Regular -ar verbs take -aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -abais, -aban; -er and -ir verbs take -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían. Only ser (era), ir (iba) and ver (veía) are irregular.
examples: De niño vivía en el campo.
Íbamos a la playa cada verano.

probes.prompt: Complete: De pequeña, ella ___ al fútbol. (jugar)
Complete: De niño, yo ___ en el campo. (vivir)
Complete: Nosotros ___ al parque cada domingo. (ir)

concepts.name: Comparatives and superlatives
concepts.description: Más que, menos que, tan como, mejor, peor and el más.
concepts.explanation: Compare with más ... que, menos ... que and tan ... como. Bueno and malo have irregular comparatives, mejor and peor. The superlative is el, la, los or las plus más plus the adjective: la más alta.
examples: Ana es más alta que Luis.
Este libro es tan interesante como ese.

practice.prompt: Complete: Mi hermano es ___ joven que yo. (less)

probes.prompt: Complete: Ana es ___ alta que Luis. (more)
Complete: Este libro es ___ interesante como ese. (as)

units.title: Food and shopping
units.summary: Order food, ask prices, and avoid repeating nouns with direct object pronouns.

concepts.name: Direct object pronouns
concepts.description: Lo, la, los and las to replace a direct object.
concepts.explanation: Direct object pronouns replace the thing or person that receives the action: lo, la, los, las (and me, te, nos, os). They agree with the noun they replace and go before a conjugated verb.

practice.prompt: Replace the noun: Bebo la leche. → ___ bebo.

probes.prompt: Replace the noun: Veo a María. → ___ veo.
Replace the noun: Compro el pan. → ___ compro.
Replace the noun: Tengo las llaves. → ___ tengo.

concepts.name: Ordering food and asking prices
concepts.description: Restaurant and shop phrases: quisiera, para mí, la cuenta, ¿cuánto cuesta?
concepts.explanation: To order politely say quisiera or para mí plus the dish; ask ¿cuánto cuesta? for one thing and ¿cuánto cuestan? for several; ask for la cuenta at the end of a meal.
examples: Quisiera un café con leche, por favor.

practice.prompt: How do you ask how much several things cost?

probes.prompt: How do you ask for 'the bill' in a restaurant?
How do you ask 'How much does it cost?' in Spanish?
Complete politely: ___ un café, por favor. (I would like)

units.title: Telling stories in the past
units.summary: Combine the preterite and the imperfect in a story, and link the past to now with the present perfect.

concepts.name: Preterite versus imperfect
concepts.description: The imperfect sets the scene; the preterite tells the events.
concepts.explanation: In a story the imperfect describes the background, what was going on and how things were, and the preterite tells the completed events that move the story on or interrupt the background.
examples: Cuando era niño, vivía en Lima.

practice.prompt: Complete: Mientras yo dormía, ___ el teléfono. (sonar)

probes.prompt: Complete: Ayer yo ___ a las ocho. (llegar)
Complete: Mientras yo ___, sonó el teléfono. (leer)
Complete: Cuando ___ niño, vivía en Lima. (ser)

concepts.name: The present perfect
concepts.description: Haber plus a past participle for experiences and events of today.
concepts.explanation: The present perfect is the present of haber (he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, han) plus a past participle ending in -ado or -ido. Common irregular participles are hecho, dicho, visto, escrito, puesto and vuelto.

units.title: Future and conditions
units.summary: Talk about the future, make polite requests and hypotheses, and set real conditions with si.

concepts.name: The simple future
concepts.description: Future endings on the infinitive, and irregular stems such as tendr- and har-.
concepts.explanation: The simple future adds -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án to the whole infinitive: hablaré, comerás. Some verbs use an irregular stem: tendré, haré, podré, saldré, diré, vendré.
examples: El año que viene viajaré a Chile.

probes.prompt: Complete: El año que viene yo ___ a Chile. (viajar)
Complete: Nosotros ___ tiempo el lunes. (tener, future)

concepts.name: The conditional
concepts.description: Would-forms for polite requests, advice and hypotheses.
concepts.explanation: The conditional adds -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían to the infinitive, with the same irregular stems as the future: tendría, haría, podría. It softens requests and expresses what would happen.

practice.prompt: Complete: Yo en tu lugar ___ más. (estudiar, conditional)

probes.prompt: Complete: Con más dinero, ellos ___ más. (viajar, conditional)
Complete: Yo ___ un coche nuevo. (comprar, conditional)

concepts.name: Real conditions with si
concepts.description: Si plus the present, then the future or a command.
concepts.explanation: A real condition uses si plus the present tense, never the future, and then the future, the present or a command in the result: si tengo tiempo, iré.
examples: Si llueve, nos quedaremos en casa.

practice.prompt: Complete: Si ___ mañana, iremos a la playa. (hacer sol, present)

probes.prompt: Which tense follows 'si' in a real condition: present or future?
Complete: Si ___ tiempo, iré a la playa. (tener, yo)
Complete: Si llueve, ___ en casa. (nosotros, quedarse, future)

units.title: Wishes, advice and opinions
units.summary: Form the present subjunctive and use it after wishes, recommendations and doubt.

concepts.name: Present subjunctive forms
concepts.description: Forming the present subjunctive from the yo form, and its irregular verbs.
concepts.explanation: The present subjunctive takes the yo form of the present, drops -o and adds the opposite vowel: -ar verbs take -e (hable), -er and -ir verbs take -a (coma, tenga). Irregular forms are sea, vaya, haya, sepa, esté and dé.

concepts.name: Subjunctive after wishes and advice
concepts.description: Quiero que, espero que and te recomiendo que with the subjunctive.
concepts.explanation: When one person wants, hopes or recommends that another person does something, the second verb goes in the subjunctive after que: quiero que vengas, espero que estéis bien, te recomiendo que bebas agua. With one subject use the infinitive: quiero venir.

concepts.name: Opinions and doubt
concepts.description: Creo que with the indicative; no creo que and dudo que with the subjunctive.
concepts.explanation: Creo que and pienso que state an opinion and take the indicative. When the opinion is negative or doubtful, no creo que, no pienso que and dudo que take the subjunctive.

probes.prompt: Which mood follows 'dudo que': indicative or subjunctive?
Complete: No creo que ___ razón. (tú, tener)

units.title: Giving instructions
units.summary: Tell someone what to do and what not to do with tú commands.

concepts.name: Affirmative tú commands
concepts.description: Tú commands: the él form of the present, and eight irregular commands.
concepts.explanation: The affirmative tú command is usually the él form of the present: habla, come, escribe. Eight verbs are irregular: di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten, ven. Pronouns attach to the end: dímelo.

concepts.name: Negative tú commands
concepts.description: No plus the present subjunctive to tell someone not to do something.
concepts.explanation: A negative tú command is no plus the tú form of the present subjunctive: no hables, no comas, no vayas. Pronouns go before the verb: no lo digas.

practice.prompt: Give the negative tú command of 'comer'.

probes.prompt: Give the negative tú command of 'hablar'.
Give the negative tú command of 'ir'.

units.title: Object pronouns
units.summary: Use indirect object pronouns and combine them with direct object pronouns.

concepts.name: Indirect object pronouns
concepts.description: Me, te, le, nos, os and les for to whom or for whom.
concepts.explanation: Indirect object pronouns say to or for whom something is done: me, te, le, nos, os, les. Le and les are often used together with the noun they refer to: le doy un regalo a mi madre.
examples: Le doy un regalo a mi madre.

practice.prompt: Complete: ___ explico la lección a los alumnos. (to them)

probes.prompt: Complete: ___ doy un regalo a mi madre. (to her)
Complete: ___ escribo a mis amigos. (to them)

concepts.name: Double object pronouns
concepts.description: Indirect before direct, and le or les becoming se before lo, la, los, las.
concepts.explanation: When both object pronouns appear, the indirect one comes first: te lo doy. Le and les become se before lo, la, los and las: se lo doy, never le lo doy.
examples: ¿El libro? Se lo doy a Juan.

practice.prompt: Replace both objects: Les mando la carta. → ___ ___ mando.

probes.prompt: Which pronoun replaces 'le' before 'lo': se or le?
Replace both objects: Le doy el libro. → ___ ___ doy.
Replace both objects: Te compro las flores. → ___ ___ compro.

units.title: Connecting ideas
units.summary: Choose between por and para, build relative clauses, and link sentences with connectors.

concepts.name: Por versus para
concepts.description: Para for purpose, destination and deadlines; por for cause, exchange, route and duration.
concepts.explanation: Para points to a goal: purpose (para aprender), recipient (para ti), destination and deadline. Por points to a cause or a means: reason (gracias por), exchange (por diez euros), movement through a place and duration.

practice.prompt: Complete: Compré el libro ___ diez euros. (por/para)

concepts.name: Relative clauses with que, donde and quien
concepts.description: Joining sentences with que, donde and quien.
concepts.explanation: Relative pronouns join two sentences: que refers to people or things, donde to places, and quien to people after a preposition: la chica con quien hablo.
examples: El libro que leo es interesante.
Esta es la ciudad donde nací.

practice.prompt: Complete: El chico ___ vive aquí es mi primo.

probes.prompt: Complete: El libro ___ leo es interesante.
Complete: Esta es la ciudad ___ nací.
Complete: La chica con ___ hablo es mi prima. (who)

concepts.name: Discourse connectors
concepts.description: Sin embargo, además, por eso, aunque and porque to link ideas.
concepts.explanation: Connectors link ideas in speech and writing: además adds, sin embargo contrasts, aunque concedes, porque gives a reason and por eso gives a consequence.
examples: Estaba cansado; sin embargo, fui a la fiesta.
Llovía, por eso me quedé en casa.

practice.prompt: How do you say 'also, in addition' at the start of a sentence?

probes.prompt: Which word means 'although': aunque or porque?
How do you say 'however' in Spanish?
How do you say 'that is why' in Spanish?
